Issued at 246 PM CDT Thu Oct 15 2026

...Synopsis...

Widespread stratus is present across the area this afternoon,
both head of and behind the surface cold front that is moving 
through the region. Satellite imagery suggests extensive 
upstream stratus will prevail through much of tonight, save for 
across the Devils Lake Basin where some late-night clearing is 
expected. Showers are developing in southern Manitoba and north
central ND in cyclonic flow, and are expected to spread south- 
southeast through this evening, resulting in a high PoP/low QPF 
scenario as the primary middle- and upper-level shortwave trough
axis crosses the region. In the wake of this wave, mean upper- 
level ridging is forecast to build into the region by this 
weekend and is forecast to remain in place through much of next 
week. Low-level warm air advection this weekend will result in 
above-normal temperatures beginning Saturday and continuing 
through the middle to latter parts of next week. The spread in 
ensemble guidance and NBM membership is small for most of this 
period, with high confidence in highs in the 60s across much of 
the area from Saturday through next Thursday. Guidance suggests 
that a weakening shortwave trough and cold front may move 
through late this weekend, with breezy south-southwest winds 
ahead of that on Saturday, and breezy northwest winds behind it 
on Sunday. A mainly dry forecast is also in place from Friday 
through the middle to late part of next week given the mean 
ridging, though a low to medium probability exists for flow 
aloft to turn southwest by the middle of next week, which may 
eventually predicate low rain chances by then.

...Strong Winds through Tonight...

Northwest winds gusting up to 35 to 45 mph this afternoon are 
forecast to turn northerly and increase further tonight, with
gusts of 40 to 50 mph, particularly in the Red River valley.
Surface low pressure is centered near Lake of the Woods as of
early afternoon, with a trailing cold front southwestward into 
west central MN. The surface low and cold front are both 
forecast to continue moving east-southeast across the area by 
late afternoon. Initial low- and midlevel cold air advection and
an increasing surface pressure gradient behind the front is 
contributing to gusty winds in eastern North Dakota, which may 
approach advisory criteria from the Devils Lake Basin southward 
toward Valley City before 00z. However, the initial push of 
cold air advection is not particularly long-lived, and surface 
pressure rises are lacking. Both of those aspects will change 
after 00z when the middle- and upper-level shortwave trough axis
passes eastern ND, turning deep-layer flow to a northerly 
direction, with a secondary and stronger surge of cold air 
advection concurrent with increasing deep-layer subsidence. The 
low-level wind fields will also increase with 45-50 kt flow in 
the 925 to 850 mb layer and cold-air-advection-steepened lapse 
rates contributing to sufficient mixing and momentum transfer 
through much of that layer. We also anticipate a 5-7 mb/3 hour 
surface pressure rise bubble moving southward through eastern ND
and far western MN. This scenario is expected to yield 
advisory-level north-northwest winds in those areas, maximized 
in the Red River Valley given the orientation of the flow. Point
forecast soundings at both Grand Forks and Fargo suggest 
momentum transfer may be sufficient for 50 kt gusts, but the 
depth and temporal efficiency of the mixed layer was not 
sufficient for us to upgrade to a High Wind Warning. Having said
that, there is a 30-50% chance of gusts reaching 60 mph in the 
Red River Valley tonight when the aforementioned ingredients 
align, particularly in the 02z to 07z time frame. Both time- 
lagged HRRR and 12z RRFS/REFS guidance support maximum gusts 
near 50 mph, consistent with some uncertainty in the depth of 
mixing. 

There is also around a 50% probability that advisory-level gusts 
extend further into west central MN, e.g., portions of Otter Tail 
and Grant Counties. Time-lagged HRRR guidance supports that 
potential, but with some uncertainty in mixing nocturnally, we
have not yet added them into the Wind Advisory.

Winds are forecast to rapidly diminish by Friday morning as a 
surface ridge axis begins to approach the area.

...Freezing Temperatures...

We have issued a Freeze Warning for portions of the area centered
on the Devils Lake Basin tonight, where ensemble guidance and 
upstream observations provide high confidence in overnight lows 
in the upper 20s to lower 30s F. This is supported by expected
low-level cold air advection, but may be offset by lingering 
clouds (stratus) and winds that may not diminish until close to 
sunset even in those areas. Across the remainder of eastern ND 
and northwest and west central MN, we believe the cloud cover 
and winds will tend to inhibit the efficiency of cooling. Taken
